title: Deterministic Replay & Operator Safety Manifest
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview:

This document defines a deterministic replay pipeline and the operator safety contract used to validate kernel/operator changes before and during runtime rollouts. The goal is to enable repeatable repros for latency/correctness regressions, reduce time-to-diagnosis for oncall, and provide a standardized canary + rollback procedure for experimental kernels and scheduler policies.

Scope:
- Deterministic capture and replay for text-generation and chat request surfaces (hosted + dedicated pools).
- Canary orchestration for kernel/operator binary changes and scheduler policy updates.
- Safety checks and telemetry contract required for any kernel-level change deployed to production.

Non-goals:
- Full deterministic replay of external tool/plugin side-effects (these are captured best-effort).
- Replaying privacy-sensitive payloads outside of secure reproducer environments.

Design summary:
1) Capture: lightweight per-request snapshot containing request proto, sequence tokens (first N tokens), model variant, session KV hints, scheduler decisions, and kernel hints. Captures are sampled at adjustable rates (default 0.1%). All captures are salted and stored in an encrypted replay store with access controls.

2) Canonicalization: a reproducible normalization step strips reorder-insignificant metadata (timestamps, trace ids) and pins kernel-versioned artifacts so that the replay input deterministically maps to kernel behavior.

3) Replay harness: an isolated, deterministic executor that replays a captured request on a pinned model binary with seeded RNG, fixed batch shapes, and a frozen scheduler policy. Replays run in a shadow environment that mirrors runtime kernel flags used in production.

4) Diffing & Triage: replay output (token stream + timings + kernel trace) is diffed against the original recorded output. Differences are classified with signatures (content-drift, timing-regression, soft-failure, hard-failure).

Deterministic capture schema (summary table):
| field | description | retention |
|---|---|---|
| capture_id | UUID for replay artifact | 90d |
| trace_version | schema version | 90d |
| request_proto | sanitized request payload (PII removed) | 90d |
| seed_state | RNG/initial-state for model runtime | 90d |
| kernel_hints | kernel invocation metadata (flags/kernels used) | 90d |
| scheduler_decision | assigned slot, priority bucket | 90d |
| sample_metrics | timing, memory usage summary | 90d |

Operator safety checklist (required before any kernel/operator rollout):
- Preconditions:
  - Unittest suite coverage for changed operator >= 95% of modified code paths.
  - Microbenchmarks for tight loops created and committed to perf-suite.
  - Static analysis & ASAN/TSAN pass for proposed patch.
- Canary plan:
  - Canary cohort definition (tenant list or synthetic traffic) 
  - Canary duration: minimum 72 hours real traffic + 24 hours synthetic stress.
  - Acceptance thresholds defined (see SLOs table below).
- Observability & Telemetry:
  - Kernel must emit the agreed telemetry keys (kernel.execution_time_ms, kernel.exec_count, kernel.error_code, kernel.fidelity_tag).
  - Trace sampling rate for capture increased to 1% for canary window.
  - Alert hooks configured for anomaly conditions (automated rollback triggers).
- Rollback strategy:
  - Immediate circuit-breaker if any hard-failure signature observed in >0.01% of canary requests.
  - Staged rollback (canary -> cohort -> global) via policy manager.

Canary runbook (step-by-step):
1. Prepare artifacts:
  1.1 Build kernel binary with embedded build-id and deterministic metadata.
  1.2 Publish to artifact-repo with tag: canary/<ticket>-<date>.
  1.3 Create canary deployment in test cluster with replica_count=2, isolate networking.
2. Pre-flight checks (automated):
  2.1 Run unit & microbench pipelines (must pass).
  2.2 Run golden replays for 50 representative captures (zero content deviation allowed).
3. Start canary (rolling):
  3.1 Route 0.5% production traffic to canary cohort and enable replay capture at 1% sampling.
  3.2 Monitor KPIs for the first 30 minutes: tail-99 latency, kernel.exec_time_ms p99, error_count.
4. Escalation and rollback policies:
  4.1 If any of the automated checks trigger (see thresholds) perform immediate rollback and mark change blocked.
  4.2 If degraded but within tolerance, expand to cohort-controlled ramp and continue data collection.

Telemetry contract (required metrics and labels):
| metric name | type | labels | description | alert threshold |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| kernel.execution_time_ms | gauge | kernel_version, model, hardware | per-invocation kernel time | p99 increase > 25% |
| kernel.exec_count | counter | kernel_version, model | invocations | sudden drop > 50% |
| kernel.error_code | counter | kernel_version, code | nonzero return codes | >= 1/10k hard-errors |
| kernel.memory_bytes | gauge | kernel_version, node | memory footprint | sustained increase > 20% |

Sample config snippet (replay harness) - YAML:
---
replay: 
  executor_image: "gcr.io/redwood/replay-executor:stable"
  seed: 0x9f1b2c
  isolate_network: true
  kernel_pin: "kernel-v2.11.3-canary"
  batch_shape_override: [1, 512]
  capture_store: "s3://replay-store/canaries/"
---

CLI examples:
- Trigger a golden replay set (50 captures):
  rwd-replay run --captures-file /tmp/golden50.list --executor-image gcr.io/redwood/replay-executor:stable --out /tmp/replays/
- Compare replay outputs:
  rwd-replay diff --baseline /tmp/originals --candidate /tmp/replays --report /tmp/replay-report.json

Diff classification and automated actions:
- content-drift: textual output mismatches (normalized). Action: manual triage and stop rollout if drift signature not explainable.
- timing-regression: p99 kernel.execution_time_ms increased >25% and coincident tail latency spike. Action: pause rollout; trigger performance bisect.
- soft-failure: minor error codes flagged (retries succeeded). Action: continue with expanded synthetic stress and re-evaluate in 24 hours.
- hard-failure: abort/segfault/incorrect logits. Action: immediate rollback and bug-bisect.

SLOs & thresholds (canary acceptance):
- No hard-failures: 100% for golden set.
- Content parity: >= 99.995% token-level match for golden set.
- Latency: p99 kernel.exec_time_ms increase <= 15% vs baseline.
- Memory: sustained memory increase <= 10% for 1h window.

Ownership & escalation:
- Kernel owner: @marcos-rivera (eng-serving-runtime/kernel-team) — primary oncall during rollout.
- Observability owner: @lena-huang (eng-platform/telemetry) — owns alerts and dashboard updates.
- Escalation path: kernel owner -> runtime lead -> SRE director.

Operational caveats and privacy:
- Captured requests are sanitized; any capture that contains suspected PII must be flagged and subject to restricted storage and manual review.
- Replay artifacts used for debugging outside central replay cluster must be provisioned into a short-lived isolated environment (TTL <= 7d).

Appendix: Example investigation flow (short):
1) Oncall observes p99 spike and kernel.exec_time_ms p99 delta +32%.
2) Increase replay sampling to 5% for affected pool and trigger rwd-replay run against last 1h captures.
3) Golden replays show timing-regression signature for 3 specific captures.
4) Run microbenchmark for changed operator; bisect to identify commit that introduced divergence.
5) Rollback to previous kernel tag and validate stability.
